Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Under the leadership of Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i of the _____, some 500 of them attacked Mu'awiya's camp at Nukhayla (a place outside Kufa) where he was taking the Kufans' oath of allegiance
Kharijites.fact: Under the leadership of Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i of the Banu Murra, some 500 of them attacked Mu'awiya's camp at Nukhayla (a place outside Kufa) where he was taking the Kufans' oath of allegiance.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Seven more _____ uprisings, with rebel numbers in individual revolts varying between 20 and 400, were defeated by the governor al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba
Kharijites.fact: Seven more Kufan Kharijite uprisings, with rebel numbers in individual revolts varying between 20 and 400, were defeated by the governor al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba. The best known of these revolts was that of al-Mustawrid ibn Ullafa, who was recognized as caliph by the Kufan Kharijites in 663.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: With about 300 followers, he left Kufa and moved to _____
Kharijites.fact: With about 300 followers, he left Kufa and moved to Behrasir.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: There, he confronted the deputy governor Simak ibn Ubayd al-Absi and invited him to denounce _____ and Ali "who had made innovations in the religion and denied the holy book"
Kharijites.fact: There, he confronted the deputy governor Simak ibn Ubayd al-Absi and invited him to denounce Uthman and Ali "who had made innovations in the religion and denied the holy book".

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Simak refused and al-_____, instead of engaging him directly, decided to exhaust and fragment Simak's forces by forcing them into pursuit
Kharijites.fact: The best known of these revolts was that of al-Mustawrid ibn Ullafa, who was recognized as caliph by the Kufan Kharijites in 663. Simak refused and al-Mustawrid, instead of engaging him directly, decided to exhaust and fragment Simak's forces by forcing them into pursuit.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Moving onto _____ near Basra, al-Mustawrid was overtaken by a 300-strong advance party of Simak's forces
Kharijites.fact: Moving onto Madhar near Basra, al-Mustawrid was overtaken by a 300-strong advance party of Simak's forces.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Although al-_____ was able to withstand this small force, he fled again toward Kufa when the main body of Simak's forces, under the command of Ma'qil ibn Qays, arrived
Kharijites.fact: Simak refused and al-Mustawrid, instead of engaging him directly, decided to exhaust and fragment Simak's forces by forcing them into pursuit. Moving onto Madhar near Basra, al-Mustawrid was overtaken by a 300-strong advance party of Simak's forces.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Kufan Kharijism died out around 663, and Basra became the center of _____ disturbances
Kharijites.fact: The advance guard returned in the meantime and attacked the Kharijites from the rear. Kufan Kharijism died out around 663, and Basra became the center of Kharijite disturbances.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Notable among these was that of the cousins Qarib ibn Murra al-Azdi and _____ ibn Zahr al-Tayyi
Kharijites.fact: Notable among these was that of the cousins Qarib ibn Murra al-Azdi and Zuhhaff ibn Zahr al-Tayyi.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: In 672/673, they rebelled in _____ with a 70-strong band
Kharijites.fact: Kufan Kharijism died out around 663, and Basra became the center of Kharijite disturbances. In 672/673, they rebelled in Basra with a 70-strong band.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Afterward, _____ is reported to have severely persecuted their followers
Kharijites.fact: Afterward, Ziyad is reported to have severely persecuted their followers. Ibn Ziyad jailed any Kharijite whom he suspected of being dangerous and executed several Kharijite sympathizers who had publicly denounced him.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Ibn Ziyad jailed any _____ whom he suspected of being dangerous and executed several Kharijite sympathizers who had publicly denounced him
Kharijites.fact: Ibn Ziyad jailed any Kharijite whom he suspected of being dangerous and executed several Kharijite sympathizers who had publicly denounced him. Between their successive reigns, Ziyad and his son are said to have killed 13,000 Kharijites.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Of the quietists, the best known was _____ ibn Udayya al-Tamimi
Kharijites.fact: Of the quietists, the best known was Abu Bilal Mirdas ibn Udayya al-Tamimi.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Provoked by the torture and murder of a Kharijite woman by _____, Abu Bilal abandoned Basra and revolted in 680/681 with 40 men
Kharijites.fact: Provoked by the torture and murder of a Kharijite woman by Ibn Ziyad, Abu Bilal abandoned Basra and revolted in 680/681 with 40 men.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Shortly after defeating a 2,000-strong _____ force in Ahwaz, he fell to a larger army of 3,000 or 4,000 in Fars in southern Persia
Kharijites.fact: One of the earliest Kharijites who had seceded at Siffin, he was held in the highest esteem by the Basran quietists. Shortly after defeating a 2,000-strong Basran force in Ahwaz, he fell to a larger army of 3,000 or 4,000 in Fars in southern Persia.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: His fate is said to have aroused the quietists and contributed to the increased _____ militancy in the subsequent period
Kharijites.fact: One of the earliest Kharijites who had seceded at Siffin, he was held in the highest esteem by the Basran quietists. Provoked by the torture and murder of a Kharijite woman by Ibn Ziyad, Abu Bilal abandoned Basra and revolted in 680/681 with 40 men.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The people of the Hejaz (where Mecca and _____ are located) rebelled against Mu'awiya's son and successor, Yazid
Kharijites.fact: The people of the Hejaz (where Mecca and Medina are located) rebelled against Mu'awiya's son and successor, Yazid.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The majority, including Nafi ibn al-Azraq and Najda ibn Amir al-Hanafi, _____, while the remainder left for the Yamama, in central Arabia, under the leadership of Abu Talut Salim ibn Matar
Kharijites.fact: The majority, including Nafi ibn al-Azraq and Najda ibn Amir al-Hanafi, went to Basra, while the remainder left for the Yamama, in central Arabia, under the leadership of Abu Talut Salim ibn Matar.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: In the meantime, _____ was expelled by tribal chiefs in Basra, where inter-tribal strife ensued
Kharijites.fact: In the meantime, Ibn Ziyad was expelled by tribal chiefs in Basra, where inter-tribal strife ensued. Ibn al-Azraq and other militant Kharijites took over the city, killed the deputy left by Ibn Ziyad and freed 140 Kharijites from prison.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Soon afterwards, the _____ recognized Ibn al-Zubayr, who appointed Umar ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar as the city's governor
Kharijites.fact: Soon afterwards, the Basrans recognized Ibn al-Zubayr, who appointed Umar ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar as the city's governor.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Umar drove out Ibn al-_____'s men from Basra and they escaped to Ahwaz
Kharijites.fact: Ibn al-Azraq and other militant Kharijites took over the city, killed the deputy left by Ibn Ziyad and freed 140 Kharijites from prison. Umar drove out Ibn al-Azraq's men from Basra and they escaped to Ahwaz.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: An army sent against them by the _____ governor of Basra in early 685 defeated the Azariqa, and Ibn al-Azraq was killed
Kharijites.fact: An army sent against them by the Zubayrid governor of Basra in early 685 defeated the Azariqa, and Ibn al-Azraq was killed. The Azariqa chose Ubayd Allah ibn Mahuz as their new leader, regrouped, forced the Zubayrid army to retreat, and resumed their raids.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: After more defeats, Ibn al-_____ deployed his most able commander, Muhallab ibn Abi Sufra, against the Azariqa
Kharijites.fact: An army sent against them by the Zubayrid governor of Basra in early 685 defeated the Azariqa, and Ibn al-Azraq was killed. The Azariqa chose Ubayd Allah ibn Mahuz as their new leader, regrouped, forced the Zubayrid army to retreat, and resumed their raids.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The Azariqa chose _____ ibn Mahuz as their new leader, regrouped, forced the Zubayrid army to retreat, and resumed their raids
Kharijites.fact: The Azariqa chose Ubayd Allah ibn Mahuz as their new leader, regrouped, forced the Zubayrid army to retreat, and resumed their raids.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The Azariqa retreated to _____
Kharijites.fact: The Azariqa retreated to Fars.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The Azariqa plundered al-Mada'in and then besieged _____, but were defeated
Kharijites.fact: The Azariqa plundered al-Mada'in and then besieged Isfahan, but were defeated.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: They fled and eventually regrouped in _____
Kharijites.fact: They fled and eventually regrouped in Kirman. Although the Azariqa were not dislodged from Fars and Kirman, Muhallab prevented their advance into Iraq.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Reinvigorated by a new leader, Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a, the _____ attacked Basra's environs afterward and Muhallab was redeployed to suppress them
Kharijites.fact: The Azariqa plundered al-Mada'in and then besieged Isfahan, but were defeated. Reinvigorated by a new leader, Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a, the Azariqa attacked Basra's environs afterward and Muhallab was redeployed to suppress them.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Although the _____ were not dislodged from Fars and Kirman, Muhallab prevented their advance into Iraq
Kharijites.fact: The Azariqa plundered al-Mada'in and then besieged Isfahan, but were defeated. Reinvigorated by a new leader, Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a, the Azariqa attacked Basra's environs afterward and Muhallab was redeployed to suppress them.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: After the _____ reconquered Iraq from the Zubayrids in 691, Umayyad princes took over the command from Muhallab, but were dealt severe defeats by the Azariqa
Kharijites.fact: After the Umayyads reconquered Iraq from the Zubayrids in 691, Umayyad princes took over the command from Muhallab, but were dealt severe defeats by the Azariqa.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: In 694 the commander _____ ibn Yusuf was appointed governor of Iraq and reinstated Muhallab to lead the war against the Azariqa
Kharijites.fact: In 694 the commander Hajjaj ibn Yusuf was appointed governor of Iraq and reinstated Muhallab to lead the war against the Azariqa.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Muhallab forced their retreat to _____, where they split into two groups and were subsequently destroyed in 698–699
Kharijites.fact: Muhallab forced their retreat to Kirman, where they split into two groups and were subsequently destroyed in 698–699.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Najda, with his followers, moved to the Yamama, the homeland of his _____ tribe
Kharijites.fact: Najda, with his followers, moved to the Yamama, the homeland of his Banu Hanifa tribe.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: He became leader of _____'s Kharijite faction, which became known as the Najdat after him
Kharijites.fact: He became leader of Abu Talut's Kharijite faction, which became called the Najdat after him.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Najda took control of _____, repulsing a 14,000-strong Zubayrid army deployed against him
Kharijites.fact: Najda took control of Bahrayn, repulsing a 14,000-strong Zubayrid army deployed against him.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: His lieutenant, _____ ibn al-Aswad, captured Oman from the local Julanda rulers, though the latter reasserted their control after a few months
Kharijites.fact: His lieutenant, Atiyya ibn al-Aswad, captured Oman from the local Julanda rulers, though the latter reasserted their control after a few months.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Najda seized _____ and Yemen in 687 and later captured Ta'if, a town close to Ibn al-Zubayr's capital Mecca, leaving the latter cornered in the Hejaz, as Najda controlled most of Arabia
Kharijites.fact: Najda seized Hadramawt and Yemen in 687 and later captured Ta'if, a town close to Ibn al-Zubayr's capital Mecca, leaving the latter cornered in the Hejaz, as Najda controlled most of Arabia.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Atiyya had already broken from Najda and moved to _____ in eastern Persia, and was later killed there or in Sind
Kharijites.fact: Atiyya had already broken from Najda and moved to Sistan in eastern Persia, and was later killed there or in Sind. In Sistan, his followers split into various sects, including the Atawiyya and the Ajarida.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: In Sistan, his followers split into various sects, including the _____ and the Ajarida
Kharijites.fact: In Sistan, his followers split into various sects, including the Atawiyya and the Ajarida.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: In Arabia, _____ ibn Thawr took over the leadership of the Najdat and defeated several Zubayrid and later Umayyad attacks
Kharijites.fact: In Arabia, Abu Fudayk Abd Allah ibn Thawr took over the leadership of the Najdat and defeated several Zubayrid and later Umayyad attacks.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: He was eventually killed along with 6,000 followers in 692 by _____ forces in Bahrayn
Kharijites.fact: In Arabia, Abu Fudayk Abd Allah ibn Thawr took over the leadership of the Najdat and defeated several Zubayrid and later Umayyad attacks. He was eventually killed along with 6,000 followers in 692 by Umayyad forces in Bahrayn.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Politically exterminated, the _____ retreated into obscurity and disappeared around the tenth century
Kharijites.fact: In Arabia, Abu Fudayk Abd Allah ibn Thawr took over the leadership of the Najdat and defeated several Zubayrid and later Umayyad attacks. Politically exterminated, the Najdat retreated into obscurity and disappeared around the tenth century.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: All the other uncategorized _____ subgroups are considered offshoots of the Sufriyya
Kharijites.fact: A moderate group, headed by Abd Allah ibn Saffar (or Asfar) and Abd Allah ibn Ibad, disagreed with the radical Azariqa and Najdat on the question of rebellion and separation from the non-Kharijites. Ibn Saffar and Ibn Ibad then disagreed amongst themselves as to the faith of the non-Kharijites, and thus came the two other sects: the Sufriyya and Ibadiyya.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Jabir, a respected scholar and traditionist, had friendly relations with Abd al-Malik and _____
Kharijites.fact: Jabir, a respected scholar and traditionist, had friendly relations with Abd al-Malik and Hajjaj. Following the death of Abd al-Malik, relations between the Ibadiyya leaders and Hajjaj deteriorated, as the former became inclined towards activism (khuruj).

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Following the death of Abd al-Malik, relations between the _____ leaders and Hajjaj deteriorated, as the former became inclined towards activism (khuruj)
Kharijites.fact: After Ibn Ibad's death, the Ibadiyya are considered to have been led into the late Umayyad period successively by Jabir ibn Zayd and Abu Ubayda Muslim ibn Abi Karima. Following the death of Abd al-Malik, relations between the Ibadiyya leaders and Hajjaj deteriorated, as the former became inclined towards activism (khuruj).

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Hajjaj consequently exiled some of them to _____ and imprisoned others
Kharijites.fact: Hajjaj consequently exiled some of them to Oman and imprisoned others.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Abu Ubayda, who was released after the death of Hajjaj in 714, became the next leader of the _____
Kharijites.fact: Following the death of Abd al-Malik, relations between the Ibadiyya leaders and Hajjaj deteriorated, as the former became inclined towards activism (khuruj). Abu Ubayda, who was released after the death of Hajjaj in 714, became the next leader of the Ibadiyya.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: After unsuccessfully attempting to win over the _____ caliphs to the Ibadi doctrine, he sent missionaries to propagate the doctrine in different parts of the empire
Kharijites.fact: After unsuccessfully attempting to win over the Umayyad caliphs to the Ibadi doctrine, he sent missionaries to propagate the doctrine in different parts of the empire.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Almost simultaneously, the _____ also spread into North Africa and southern Arabia through missionary activity
Kharijites.fact: Almost simultaneously, the Sufriyya also spread into North Africa and southern Arabia through missionary activity. Through absorption into the Ibadiyya, the Sufriyya eventually became extinct.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Through absorption into the _____, the Sufriyya eventually became extinct
Kharijites.fact: Abu Ubayda, who was released after the death of Hajjaj in 714, became the next leader of the Ibadiyya. Through absorption into the Ibadiyya, the Sufriyya eventually became extinct.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Modern historians consider _____ to be a legendary figure, and assert that the Sufriyya and Ibadiyya sects did not exist during the seventh century
Kharijites.fact: Modern historians consider Ibn Saffar to be a legendary figure, and assert that the Sufriyya and Ibadiyya sects did not exist during the seventh century.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: As such, there was only one moderate _____ current, which might have been called "Sufri"
Kharijites.fact: Ibadi sources too are more or less in line with this scheme, where the Ibadiyya appear as the true successors of the original Medinese community and the early, pre-Second-Fitna Kharijites, though Ibn Ibad does not feature prominently and Jabir is asserted as the leader of the movement following Abu Bilal Mirdas. The heresiographers, whose aim was to categorize the divergent beliefs of the Kharijites, most likely invented the Sufriyya to accommodate those groups who did not fit neatly anywhere...

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The moderates condemned the militancy of the _____ and Najdat, but otherwise lacked a set of concrete doctrines
Kharijites.fact: The moderates condemned the militancy of the Azariqa and Najdat, but otherwise lacked a set of concrete doctrines.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Jabir and _____ may have been prominent figures in the moderate movement
Kharijites.fact: Jabir and Abu Ubayda may have been prominent figures in the moderate movement.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The moderates further split into the true _____ and Ibadiyya only during the eighth century, with the main difference being tribal affiliations rather than doctrinal differences
Kharijites.fact: The moderates further split into the true Sufriyya and Ibadiyya only during the eighth century, with the main difference being tribal affiliations rather than doctrinal differences.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: During the _____, the moderates remained inactive
Kharijites.fact: During the Second Fitna, the moderates remained inactive.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: However, in the mid-690s they also started militant activities in response to persecution by _____
Kharijites.fact: However, in the mid-690s they also started militant activities in response to persecution by Hajjaj.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The first of their revolts was led in 695 by _____, and ended in defeat and Ibn Musarrih's death
Kharijites.fact: The first of their revolts was led in 695 by Ibn Musarrih, and ended in defeat and Ibn Musarrih's death.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Afterward, this _____ group became a major threat to Kufa and its suburbs under Shabib
Kharijites.fact: Afterward, this Kharijite group became a major threat to Kufa and its suburbs under Shabib.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: With a small army of a few hundred warriors, Shabib defeated several thousands-strong _____ armies in 695–696, looted Kufa's treasury and occupied al-Mada'in
Kharijites.fact: With a small army of a few hundred warriors, Shabib defeated several thousands-strong Umayyad armies in 695–696, looted Kufa's treasury and occupied al-Mada'in.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: From his base in al-Mada'in, _____ moved to capture Kufa
Kharijites.fact: Afterward, this Kharijite group became a major threat to Kufa and its suburbs under Shabib. With a small army of a few hundred warriors, Shabib defeated several thousands-strong Umayyad armies in 695–696, looted Kufa's treasury and occupied al-Mada'in.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Hajjaj had already requested _____ troops from Abd al-Malik, who sent a 4,000-strong army which defeated Shabib outside Kufa
Kharijites.fact: Hajjaj had already requested Syrian troops from Abd al-Malik, who sent a 4,000-strong army which defeated Shabib outside Kufa.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: During the last days of the _____ empire, a major Sufri revolt erupted in Iraq in 744
Kharijites.fact: During the last days of the Umayyad empire, a major Sufri revolt erupted in Iraq in 744. At this stage even some Umayyad officials, including two sons of former caliphs (Sulayman, son of Hisham and Abd Allah, son of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz), recognized him as caliph and joined his ranks.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: At this stage even some _____ officials, including two sons of former caliphs (Sulayman, son of Hisham and Abd Allah, son of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz), recognized him as caliph and joined his ranks
Kharijites.fact: During the last days of the Umayyad empire, a major Sufri revolt erupted in Iraq in 744. At this stage even some Umayyad officials, including two sons of former caliphs (Sulayman, son of Hisham and Abd Allah, son of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz), recognized him as caliph and joined his ranks.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: It was at first led by Sa'id ibn Bahdal al-_____, and after his death from plague, Dahhak ibn Qays al-Shaybani
Kharijites.fact: It was at first led by Sa'id ibn Bahdal al-Shaybani, and after his death from plague, Dahhak ibn Qays al-Shaybani.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Joined by many more _____ from other parts of the empire, he captured Kufa in April 745 and later Wasit, which had replaced Kufa as the regional capital under Hajjaj
Kharijites.fact: Joined by many more Sufriyya from other parts of the empire, he captured Kufa in April 745 and later Wasit, which had replaced Kufa as the regional capital under Hajjaj.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Dahhak captured Mosul, but was killed by the forces of the _____ II in 746
Kharijites.fact: Dahhak captured Mosul, but was killed by the forces of the Caliph Marwan II in 746.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: His successor, _____ ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Yashkuri, was driven out from Mosul by Marwan II and fled to Fars to join the Alid leader Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiya, who ruled in opposition to the Umayyads
Kharijites.fact: His successor, Shayban ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Yashkuri, was driven out from Mosul by Marwan II and fled to Fars to join the Alid leader Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiya, who ruled in opposition to the Umayyads. Attacked there by the Umayyads, they dispersed and Shayban fled to Oman, where he was killed by the local leaders around 751.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Attacked there by the _____, they dispersed and Shayban fled to Oman, where he was killed by the local leaders around 751
Kharijites.fact: His successor, Shayban ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Yashkuri, was driven out from Mosul by Marwan II and fled to Fars to join the Alid leader Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiya, who ruled in opposition to the Umayyads. Attacked there by the Umayyads, they dispersed and Shayban fled to Oman, where he was killed by the local leaders around 751.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Under the _____, who had toppled the Umayyads in 750, Sufri revolts in the eastern parts of the empire continued for almost two centuries, though at a small scale and were easily put down
Kharijites.fact: Under the Abbasids, who had toppled the Umayyads in 750, Sufri revolts in the eastern parts of the empire continued for almost two centuries, though at a small scale and were easily put down. However, in revolts led by Abd al-Hamid al-Bajali in 866–877 and by Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Bajali in 880–896, the Kharijites gained control of northern Mesopotamia from the Abbasids and collected taxes.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: They were mostly of _____ origin and were recruited through missionary activity
Kharijites.fact: They were mostly of Berber origin and were recruited through missionary activity.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: With the Ibadi–Sufri distinction emergent in this period, the groups with no Ibadi affiliation were associated with the _____
Kharijites.fact: With the Ibadi–Sufri distinction emergent in this period, the groups with no Ibadi affiliation were associated with the Sufriyya. Around 740, the Sufriyya under the leadership of Maysara al-Matghari had revolted in Tangiers and captured the city from the Umayyads.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Around 740, the _____ under the leadership of Maysara al-Matghari had revolted in Tangiers and captured the city from the Umayyads
Kharijites.fact: With the Ibadi–Sufri distinction emergent in this period, the groups with no Ibadi affiliation were associated with the Sufriyya. Around 740, the Sufriyya under the leadership of Maysara al-Matghari had revolted in Tangiers and captured the city from the Umayyads.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: They marched onto the provincial capital _____, but were unable to capture it
Kharijites.fact: They marched onto the provincial capital Kairouan, but were unable to capture it.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Nevertheless, Sufri disturbances in _____ continued throughout the Umayyad period
Kharijites.fact: Nevertheless, Sufri disturbances in North Africa continued throughout the Umayyad period.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Around 750, the _____ established a dynasty in Sijilmasa, in modern Morocco
Kharijites.fact: Around 750, the Sufri Midrarids set up a dynasty in Sijilmasa, in modern Morocco.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: The dynasty survived until the _____ capture of the city in 909
Kharijites.fact: The dynasty survived until the Fatimid capture of the city in 909. Nonetheless, the Midrarids continued governing the city under intermittent Fatimid suzerainty until 976.

Kharijites.subject: Indian Society
Kharijites.question: Nonetheless, the _____ continued governing the city under intermittent Fatimid suzerainty until 976
